summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of poorly controlled type 1 diabetes, alcohol use disorder, and depression was admitted with altered mental status and severe hyperglycemia, diagnosed as diabetic ketoacidosis. She presented with vomiting, lethargy, and a blood glucose of 1465, along with hypovolemic shock, acute kidney injury, and hyperkalemia. She was treated with IV fluids, insulin infusion, and correction of electrolytes. Her hospital course was complicated by anemia requiring a blood transfusion, likely due to chronic gastrointestinal blood loss, and a Type 2 NSTEMI related to the metabolic stress of DKA. She received a central line for monitoring and treatment, and her renal function and mental status improved. She was transitioned to subcutaneous insulin with a simplified regimen and discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up including endocrinology, gastroenterology for endoscopy, and enrollment in an intensive outpatient alcohol rehabilitation program. She was prescribed naltrexone, pantoprazole, and all chronic medications, including insulin, aspirin, and metoprolol.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis without coma
Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
